One night two young men from Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals and while they were there it became foggy and calm. Then it was market night and the people from the pueblo came down to the river, kanging (the hide coverings) and making ready to trade. News! A long time ago! Then the people from the pueblo went home again, and the two young men went with them, and soon the people of the pueblo said: "These young men are our cousins." And from that time on, the people of the pueblo and the people of the village were one people.

From that time on, the people of the pueblo and the people of the village helped each other, and sometimes the people of the pueblo would give the people of the village things, and sometimes the people of the village would give the people of the pueblo things. The people of the pueblo were glad to give things to the people of the village, because the people of the village were good workers.

One night two young men from Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals and while they were there it became foggy and calm. Then the water rose, the tide came in, and the two men were left on an island of grass. Their fire went out, and they could not find another match. One of the men took off his belt and wrapped it around the other man's neck, and they lay down on the grass and waited for morning. But in the night the tide went out, and the current dragged one of the men out to the sea. The other man waited until dawn, then he went home and told the people on the reserve that his brother had been taken by the water-spirit. And that is why, to this day, the natives of Egulac never go out to hunt seals without taking a match with them. (From "River Under the Moon", 1981)  This is a story by Northwest Coast artist and writer Mungo Martin. It is one of a series of stories that were inspired by the art of the Indigenous peoples of the Northwest Coast of North America.

One night two young men from Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals and while they were there it became foggy and calm. Then it was market night and the town was all lit up. Suddenly, the people near the shore saw a light out on the water and then they saw two forms walking on the water, coming near to the shore. Some people thought they were apparitions and others said they were the Mollemen, but in any case they went to the mission to report what they had seen.

The old chief was there and he said he would go and see for himself. He put on his cloak and went out on the road by the river, but he never came back. For three days the people waited and then they went to look for him along the river, but he was not there. Then they went to look for the two young men who had gone out to hunt seals, but they were not there either. They went to the place where the old chief had gone and there were two canoes, one larger than the other. In the larger canoe was the old chief, and in the other was a young man who was alive but who could not speak.

The people were amazed and did not know what to think. Then the Mollemen came and took the young man away and said he would be all right. Afterward the old chief's spirit came to the people and told them that he had gone to help his son and that he was now dead. He said that the Mollemen had come to take him away because he had helped the people so often that they wanted to take him away from them. He said that the young man would be all right, that he would live, but that he would never speak again. He said that the Mollemen were very powerful and that they could make a man alive again, but that they would never speak.

Then he said that he was going to live with the Mollemen and that he would never come back

One night two young men from Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals and while they were there it became foggy and calm. Then the wind rose, and the water began to chill. One of the men took off his mask, and soon after that, the other one did the same. Just then a canoe came up and two men from the village of Wickanish pulled in. "What happened?" one of them asked. "We thought we heard voices," said the other. The two men from Egulac said nothing for a long time. Then one of them spoke. "Some people," he said, "think that the world was made in six days. I used to think that too, but now I'm not so sure." He pointed towards the river. "Look at that," he said. "The world didn't just happen. It evolved. It has been evolving for a long, long time, and it will keep on evolving."  from "The Two Young Men from Egulac" by Richard Wagamese.

One night two young men from Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals and while they were there it became foggy and calm. Then the women of the tribe came down to the shore to join them, and they made a great fire on the beach, and seated themselves in a circle around it, and sang their songs, and the seals came into the beach and the young men killed them. And after this the women went up country, and the young men remained to take the seals to the village.
The next night, or perhaps it was two nights later, the women returned to the beach, and the young men went with them. And the women took up the bones of the seals and threw them into the fire, and the young men went out to hunt, and at noon they returned and ate the roes and the intestines of the seals. Thus they spent two days at the village, and then the women went up country, and the young men remained on the beach, and the next day they went out to hunt, and in the afternoon they came back and told the old men that they had killed a bear.
Now it was the bear that the old men had been waiting for. They were glad when the young men told them that they had killed a bear, and they asked them where they had seen him. The young men said that they had seen him on the hill, and the old men told them that the bear was the chief of the animals, and that he lived on the hill, and that he was very powerful and very wise.
Then the old men said to the young men: "You have done well in killing the bear. Now you must go and get the bear's bone, and bring it to us, and we will make it into a charm, and then we will be able to do great things with it."
So the young men went and got the bear's bone, and they brought it to the old men, and the old men made it into a charm

One night two young men from Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals and while they were there it became foggy and calm. Then the wind came up and there was a great storm: the waves were huge and the thunder was loud. One of the young men was afraid and he called out to his brother, "What shall we do? Let us go to the shore and make our way back through the woods."
But the other brother was not afraid. "There is no cause for fear," he said. "The storm will soon be over. Let us wait and see what happens."
So they waited and soon the wind began to calm down. Then the sun came out and shone down on the water again. "Now we have nothing to fear," said the second brother. "The storm is over and the seals are coming up around the edge of the ice."
As they took their kayaks to paddle out to the seals, the first brother saw something moving in the water. "What is that?" he asked. "I think it is a whale," his brother answered. "How can you tell?" asked the first brother. "By the way it is moving," replied the second. "Whales do not move like seals. They have a different kind of movement. Now paddle out there and see for yourself."
So they paddled out to where the whale was, and there was one, a big one. "Now do you believe?" asked the second brother. "Yes, I believe," answered the first. "Believe in what?" "Believe in the Great Spirit," said the second. "He is the one who made the whale. He is the one who made the storm. He is the one who will see us through the storm."
"But how did you know that?" asked the first brother. "I just knew it," replied the second.

One night two young men from Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals and while they were there it became foggy and calm. Then the wind blew up and there was a great storm: the waves were so high the two young men couldn't keep their heads above the water. They were exhausted from swimming and fighting the current.
One of the young men noticed a boat coming up along the shore. He called out to the people in the boat, "What are you doing here?" The people in the boat said, "We are sent by the chief of Egulac to help you."
The two young men climbed into the boat, which then went back to the shore. The people in the boat were the chief and the shaman. The chief said, "I will make you a law that will protect the Egulac people and will keep the peace. From this day on, Egulac will be a peaceful village."
From that day on, the village was known as Egulac, and the people lived in peace.
